title: One Stand-Alone Drug Plan at a Time on the Ridgecrest RxSecure Plans
content:
1. A member may hold only one stand-alone Part D prescription drug plan at a time, because Medicare allows only one drug plan election to be in force in any coverage month. The maximum number of stand-alone Part D drug plan enrollments one member may hold at once is 1.

2. Before a new Ridgecrest RxSecure stand-alone Medicare Part D prescription drug plan election is recorded, no other stand-alone Part D enrollment for the same member is submitted, awaiting the CMS transaction reply, in force, or in its premium grace period on the day the new election is recorded. The condition is settled on the plan's own enrollment records for that member, read before the election is recorded; the member's own account of what they hold is not the authority for it.

3. Where such an enrollment does exist, the new election is recorded as a plan change: the earlier enrollment ends on the day before the new coverage begins, so the member is never left without drug coverage for a day and never billed twice for one month.

4. Enrollments for different contract years that do not overlap are not duplicates, and a member's history may show several ended drug plans.

5. A member who asks to keep two drug plans at once is refused and told why, because Medicare will not accept the second election.

## Points of judgement

| What the member's enrollment record shows | Whether it blocks a new election |
| --- | --- |
| A stand-alone Part D enrollment submitted and not yet transmitted | yes |
| A stand-alone Part D enrollment awaiting the CMS transaction reply | yes |
| A stand-alone Part D enrollment in force | yes |
| A stand-alone Part D enrollment in its premium grace period | yes |
| A stand-alone Part D enrollment for an earlier contract year that has ended and does not overlap | no |

The four statuses in the table are read as at the day the new election is recorded, and the enrollments compared are those of the same member.
